observations: real_tool.case_axi_ddr_interface failed because the simulation source-identity hash, Vivado-export compile authority, ordered-command authority references, and simulator executable authorization do not bind the current exact sample-project identity. This is a board verification/integration-contract failure, not a demonstrated DUT defect.

functional_sim=fail is dependency-derived because case_vcs_functional_sim was not run while case_axi_ddr_interface failed. The absent semantic-evidence and dynamic reports are downstream evidence gaps and cannot establish a model, numeric, loader, AXI, DDR, ordering, liveness, or output-frontier failure.

CCTG debug closure reports a verification_capability_gap with no failed boundary, no failing transaction boundary value, and no root candidate module. It explicitly blocks hardware boundary tracing until the semantic capability and harness binding are repaired.

Prior repair feedback identifies a second verifier capability gap: the completed VCS compile was followed by remote_tool_failure/exit 1 without raw terminal tail, signal, timeout/kill, wall-time, or simulation-cycle provenance. Missing completion reports therefore cannot be attributed to a board adapter, testbench schema, loader, pipeline, AXI, DDR, or DUT source defect.

Hash-validated lower layers remain reusable: operator-leaf and connected single-layer certificates are live, and the connected kernel retains its certified elastic variable-latency ordering and cross-token overlap invariants. There is no current direct contradiction requiring lower-layer reopening.

The authoritative SACG truth has active same-scope contamination barriers 0329, 0330, 0331, 0341, 0342, 0343 through 0352 and open retry requests 0136, 0140 through 0144. They block downstream promotion and must remain untrusted until a fresh, fully passing Stage7 candidate is promoted; open_backtrack_request_count is zero.
The conditional design-team review was no_split and provides no substitute for deterministic tool evidence.
proposed_actions: Repair only the board-simulation manifest/compile-plan binding generator against the already discovered exact sample-project and Vivado-export evidence; do not modify wrapper RTL, connected-kernel RTL, golden outputs, weights, stimulus, or tolerances.
Rerun the failed case_axi_ddr_interface gate on the candidate binding before permitting VCS execution.
Obtain approval to implement the missing remote VCS termination-provenance runner/analyzer capability, then execute a fresh hash-bound VCS replay using the immutable semantic contract.

If and only if the replay yields a classified simulator/DUT failure, collect a current board boundary trace and CCTG causal slice before any bounded wrapper/runtime repair. Reopen a lower layer only on a direct trace contradiction of a named live certificate invariant.

After a passing VCS replay, run the remaining Stage7 DAG and semantic-evidence assembly in dependency order. Reconcile SACG retries and contamination barriers only after all required current-candidate checks pass.
risks: Changing the exact wrapper, sample-project sources, checkpoint, stimulus, target-model reference, numeric comparison policy, tolerance, or generated semantic-testbench contract would contaminate the repair loop and invalidate comparison evidence.

Using an uncited or guessed simulator executable, top module, source list, Vivado export context, or board wrapper would repeat the identity-binding failure. Ambiguous discovery facts require bounded approval rather than name or path guessing.

Without termination provenance, an external kill, timeout, remote runner failure, simulator fatal, and DUT failure are confounded; any RTL, AXI, DDR, loader, analyzer, or testbench patch made from the current runtime result would be speculative.
Board-level progress must distinguish independent AXI/prefetch progress from lifecycle/output-frontier progress. A frontier symptom alone cannot reopen the certified connected kernel.

Cross-layer consistency remains at risk across checkpoint/model scope, tensor shapes, immutable numeric policy, deterministic stimulus order, complete loader weight consumption, memory/address mapping, runtime scheduling, implementation source identity, and exact board-wrapper facts. Transformer-block verification excludes embedding/tokenization, final norm, LM head/logits, sampling, and all model-tail work.
The existing active barriers and retries prevent backend synthesis, implementation, bitstream, runtime-ABI release, and board-runtime promotion even if an isolated static checker is later repaired.

verification capability gap must be repaired before hardware trace
